notes:
ROUTE: the OpenAI API account had no credits (2 calls, HTTP 429 credit_balance_exhausted, $0). Switched to the Codex CLI (0.154) and its built-in image_gen tool on the ChatGPT subscription, so there is no marginal USD cost. The model the user named, gpt-6-luna, is refused for ChatGPT-account Codex (HTTP 400), so the runs used the config.toml default (gpt-6-astra, reasoning high). The image tool is the same either way. Each run's prompt tells Codex to cp the PNG into gpt/raw/; it did every time, so the generated_images fallback was never needed.
DELIVERED = approach 2 (single): one Codex session made six images, 460 s total (about 75 s per image). Codex's image_gen handed back genuinely transparent 1254x1254 RGBA with clean soft alpha, so no keying was needed: just trim, centre to 80%, and make a luminance-grey copy. It is the best-looking set: glossy, polished, mobile-game style, and clean on both the dark and the light strip.
Approach 1 (sheet, one image, 87-109 s): the art is equally nice but smaller per sprite (512 px cells). The tool also attached a crude blocky alpha matte, which is ignored: the cut flattens onto black and keys from brightness. Round 1 had stray sparks and debris around flame, leaf and star; round 2's prompt ("no extra particles, no dark outline") fixed the debris. The dark drawn outline on droplet and leaf still leaves a thin rim after black keying. The best cut is droplet keyed as a glow and leaf keyed solid at threshold 0.45 (flags --solid leaf --solid-thr 0.45); that result is in gpt/sheet/ for comparison.
Per sprite (single): flame good, clean tip, warm core. Droplet excellent, glossy highlight, reads at small size. Leaf excellent, midrib and stem. Bolt good, thin jagged zigzag with glow; as grey it is faint on the light strip, which is expected for a white tintable sprite. Star excellent, long 4-point with halo. Wisp good, soft violet swirl, slightly busy inner curl detail.
Repeatability: a NEW sprite is one more Codex run (~75 s, a one-line description plus the shared style) followed by `cut-single`. Style stays consistent across sprites because the style text is shared. Codex runs are not seeded, so a re-run gives a different drawing.
